statement_utf8: Let $M_0$ be a hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with isolated point singularities modeled on regular hypercones, and let $(M_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a mean curvature flow with initial data $M_0$. For any tangent flow $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ to $(M_t)_{t\ge 0}$ at a singular point $p$, one has $P_t=\sqrt{t}\,P$ for every $t>0$. The expander $P$ solves $\vec H-\frac{x^\perp}{2}=0$ for $x\in P$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Universal over initial conical hypersurfaces, flows and tangent flows; weak-flow class, multiplicity and initial-time tangent convention are unspecified.
technical_assessment: Initial-time forward blow-ups need an expander monotonicity mechanism; ordinary backward shrinker monotonicity does not prove the displayed forward identity. No short full-scope route.

statement_utf8:
Conjecture: Let $k$ be a global function field with $\\operatorname{char}(k)=2$. Then every affine algebraic $k$-group scheme has finite class numbers; that is, for every finite set $S$ of places of $k$ and every compact open subgroup $K\subset G(\mathbb A_k^S)$, the double-coset space
\[
G(k)\backslash G(\mathbb A_k)/G(k_S)K
\]
is finite.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every characteristic-two global function field, affine group scheme, finite S and compact open K; empty S and finite-type/smoothness conventions need source confirmation.
technical_assessment: Reduction to reductive groups leaves characteristic-two wound unipotent groups; a reductive class-number theorem alone is not a bridge for all affine group schemes.

statement_utf8: For every point $y:\operatorname{Spec}(F)\to N$, each tensor $t_\alpha$ ($\alpha\in J$) is the crystalline realization of an algebraic cycle on the abelian variety $A$ associated with $y$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Universal y and alpha, but N,F,J,t_alpha and the associated A are not specified.
technical_assessment: Cannot tell which crystalline tensors or integral model is intended. Restoring these data is necessary before a cycle-construction argument can be assessed.

statement_utf8: Let $G$ be a locally compact second countable Hausdorff group. If the Bost conjecture is true for $G$ and arbitrary separable $C^*$-coefficients, then the same is true for all open subgroups of $G$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every locally compact second countable Hausdorff G and every open subgroup, for all separable coefficients; Bost assembly map is not defined.
technical_assessment: Induction of coefficients is a plausible published permanence mechanism, but requires the precise L1 completion and assembly naturality; no independent new theorem claimed.

statement_utf8: Let $G$ be a locally compact second countable Hausdorff group and let $H$ be a closed subgroup of $G$. If the Bost conjecture with arbitrary separable $C^*$-algebra coefficients is true for $G$, must it also be true for $H$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every G and closed H, uniformly over separable coefficients; the Bost conjecture is an external definition.
technical_assessment: Closed-subgroup induction needs analytic comparison unavailable from open-subgroup arguments alone. A proof for discrete or open H would be only an instance.

statement_utf8: Let $G$ and $H$ be locally compact Hausdorff groupoids admitting Haar systems and having $\c3$-compact unit spaces. If $G$ and $H$ are equivalent, then the Bost conjecture with arbitrary $C^*$-coefficients is true for $G$ if and only if it is true for $H$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Universal equivalent Haar groupoids and coefficients, but the unit-space hypothesis is corrupted as c3-compact.
technical_assessment: Do not silently replace the corrupted condition by sigma-compactness; equivalence bimodule and assembly compatibility would still require a long analytic chain.

statement_utf8:
Let $A$ and $B$ be separable nuclear continuous $C(X)$-algebras over a finite-dimensional compact metrizable space $X$. If $\sigma \in KK_X(A,B)$, then
\[
\sigma \in KK_X(A,B)^{-1}\quad\text{if and only if}\quad \sigma_x \in KK(A(x),B(x))^{-1}\ \text{for all }x\in X.
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every finite-dimensional compact metrizable X, separable nuclear continuous C(X)-algebras A,B and every sigma in KK_X; invertibility iff all fiber classes invertible.
technical_assessment: Necessity follows by fiber functors; sufficiency requires global KK gluing over finite-dimensional bases. Pointwise inverses alone do not glue by a finite certificate.

statement_utf8: Is every unital properly infinite C*-algebra K1-injective; equivalently, is the canonical map $U(A)/U_0(A)\to K_1(A)$ injective for every unital properly infinite C*-algebra $A$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every unital properly infinite C*-algebra A; kernel of the canonical component-to-K1 map must vanish.
technical_assessment: Stable cancellation of unitaries is the obstruction: proper infiniteness does not supply an immediate homotopy in A. Matrix examples cannot settle all A.

statement_utf8: **Conjecture 3.** Let $f:X\to Y$ be an algebraic fiber space, i.e. $X$ and $Y$ are smooth projective varieties and $f$ is surjective with connected fibers. Then, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, the sheaf $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(mK_{X/Y})$ is globally generated outside the discriminant locus of $f$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every smooth projective fiber space and all sufficiently large m, depending on f; ground field and characteristic are absent.
technical_assessment: Weak positivity does not imply global generation without twisting. An isotrivial example would need exact monodromy analysis; no valid full-scope construction established.

statement_utf8: For every $d\in\mathbb{N}$ there is $N=N(d)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, if $K$ is any field and $F$ is a finite symmetric subset of $GL_d(K)$ containing $1$, then either the product set $F^N=F\cdot\ldots\cdot F$ contains two elements which freely generate a nonabelian free group, or the group generated by $F$ is virtually solvable, i.e. contains a solvable subgroup of finite index.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every d exists N(d), uniformly over all fields and finite symmetric F containing 1; free pair in F^N or virtual solvability.
technical_assessment: Recognizable strong uniform Tits theorem; selected primary passage checked separately. It requires a substantial structural proof, and a short new deduction would face direct public-theorem exclusion.

primary_passage.note: Theorem 1 states the exact uniform alternative; selected statement and surrounding discussion, not full proof.

statement_utf8:
For almost every pair $(a,b)\in SU(2,\mathbb{R})$, there exists a constant $C(a,b)>0$ such that
\[
d\bigl(w(a,b),1\bigr)\ge \exp\bigl(-C(a,b)\,\ell(w)\bigr)
\]
for every nontrivial word $w\in F_2$, where $d$ is a Riemannian distance on $GL_2(\mathbb{C})$ and $\ell(w)$ is the word length. The report attributes this conjecture to Sarnak.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Almost every pair and all nontrivial free words, with pair-dependent exponential constant; SU(2,R) and the measure are not consistently specified.
technical_assessment: Real-entry SU(2) would be abelian and yield commutator identities, but interpreting a notation defect that way is not discovery credit. Intended compact SU(2) Diophantine estimates are substantially harder.

statement_utf8: For a measurable flow $T=(T_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$, define $I(T)=\{s\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}:T\text{ and }T_s=(T_{st})_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\text{ are isomorphic}\}$. Is $I(T)$ a Borel group for every measurable flow $T$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every measurable real flow; I(T) asks Borelness of its self-similarity subgroup, but measure-space and isomorphism conventions are unspecified.
technical_assessment: Borelness does not follow merely from projection of the isomorphism relation; analytic subgroups need not be Borel in general. No explicit admissible flow counterexample.

statement_utf8: Conjecture: Let $G$) be the group described in the report and let $G=\gamma_0(G)\geq\gamma_1(G)\geq\gamma_2(G)\geq\cdots$ denote its lower central series, with $\gamma_{i+1}(G)=[\gamma_i(G),G]$. Then, for every $i\geq 2$, $$[\gamma_i(G):\gamma_{i+1}(G)]=\begin{cases}8,&i\equiv 0,1\pmod 3,\\4,&i\equiv 2\pmod 3.\end{cases}$$ Equivalently, the group $G$ has finite width $3$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All i>=2 in a particular group G, but G is only described in the report.
technical_assessment: Finite nilpotent quotients cannot verify the infinite periodic index pattern without the actual presentation and a recursive structural argument.

statement_utf8: Does there exist a countably infinite group $G$ for which every finite-dimensional contractible $G$-CW-complex has a global fixed point?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Exists one countably infinite G forcing a fixed point on every finite-dimensional contractible G-CW-complex, without a fixed dimension bound.
technical_assessment: Finite cohomological dimension gives free contractible actions and cannot furnish such a group. Torsion constructions need a uniform obstruction in every finite dimension.

statement_utf8: Let $X$ be a topological space, and regard $H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)$ as an unstable module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra. If $H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)\notin U_0$, then there exists an integer $s\ge 0$ such that, for every integer $n\ge 0$, $\operatorname{Nil}_s H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)/\operatorname{Nil}_{s+1}H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)\notin U_n$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every topological X outside U0, exists s, for all n, a nilpotent-layer quotient outside Un; U_n and Nil_s filtration are not defined.
technical_assessment: Interchanging the exists s and for all n is substantive. A theorem about each finite Krull layer would require a precise filtration bridge.

statement_utf8: For any hyperbolic knot manifold $M$, we have $\#E(M)\le 10$ and $\Delta(E(M))\le 8$. Moreover, if $M\neq M_1,M_2,M_3,M_4$, then $\#E(M)\le 7$ and $\Delta(E(M))\le 5$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All hyperbolic knot manifolds with two universal bounds and stronger bounds outside four exceptions; E,Delta and M1 through M4 are absent.
technical_assessment: Cannot identify exceptional slope distances or the four manifolds from the literal. General Dehn-filling bounds do not independently settle both sharp clauses.

statement_utf8: Let $K$ be a centrally symmetric oval in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with smooth boundary, and suppose that $K$ does not admit Type $4$; equivalently, no finite family of pairwise disjoint translates of $K$ has both geometric permutations $1234$ and $2413$. Must $K$ be an ellipse? The report notes that this is considered unlikely, even if strict convexity is additionally assumed.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every smooth centrally symmetric planar oval excluding simultaneous permutations 1234 and 2413 for disjoint translates; asks whether necessarily an ellipse.
technical_assessment: A perturbation of an ellipse does not visibly preserve exclusion of a transversal order type; requires uniform configuration control rather than a sampled family.

statement_utf8: For a collection of $n$ cigars in $\[3$-space—where a cigar is the Minkowski sum of a line segment and a ball, and the cigars may have arbitrary radii—the report states that the combinatorial complexity of their union is nearly quadratic.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All n and arbitrary radii; nearly quadratic is not given an epsilon or logarithmic rate, and ambient notation is corrupted.
technical_assessment: Union boundary combinatorics require a precise feature count and degeneracy convention. Quadratic equal-radius bounds do not imply this arbitrary-radius version.

statement_utf8: For every fixed integer $d\ge 5$, the decision problem whose input is a finite simplicial complex $K$ of dimension at most $d-1$ and whose output is YES exactly when $K$ admits a piecewise-linear embedding into $\mathbb{R}^d$ is algorithmically undecidable; equivalently, $\mathrm{EMBED}_{d-1\to d}$ is algorithmically undecidable.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every fixed d>=5; undecidability for all finite complexes of dimension <=d-1 embedding PL in R^d.
technical_assessment: Requires a uniform undecidability reduction, not testing finite complexes. No bounded calculation can establish the claimed algorithmic impossibility.

statement_utf8:
For every integer dimension $d\ge 3$ and every compact smooth convex surface $\partial K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with everywhere non-vanishing Gaussian curvature, one has
\[
\#\bigl(\mathbb{Z}^d\cap R\partial K\bigr)\lesssim R^{d-2}
\]
for dilations $R\to\infty$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Each d>=3 and each compact smooth positively curved convex boundary; asymptotic O_K,d(R^(d-2)) lattice count for all large R.
technical_assessment: Spherical examples reduce to exact representation-number bounds and can stress logarithmic losses, but general smooth-boundary lattice concentration has no short route established here.

statement_utf8: Is it true that $\delta(K)=\delta^*(K)$ for every convex body $K$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every convex body K; delta and delta-star packing or covering densities are undefined.
technical_assessment: Different standard density conventions yield different questions; no inequality or counterexample can be credited without restoring the two functionals.

statement_utf8: Prove that the two candidate configurations found in the reported search—one with 40 points in $\mathbb{R}^{10}$ and one with 64 points in $\mathbb{R}^{14}$—are examples of previously unknown universally optimal spherical codes.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Two configurations of 40 and 64 points in specified dimensions, but coordinates or Gram matrices are missing.
technical_assessment: Universal optimality needs exact energy comparison for every completely monotone potential; cardinality and dimension do not specify either certificate.

statement_utf8: Can the local Helly-type result for an isolated line transversal be generalized to arbitrary collections of disjoint convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Arbitrary disjoint convex sets in R^d, but the local Helly result to be generalized is absent.
technical_assessment: No Helly number, isolation condition or proposed conclusion is supplied, so an honest full-scope target cannot be extracted from this literal.

statement_utf8: Does there exist a universal constant $d_0$ such that every finite projective plane, considered as a set system $(X,\mathcal F)$, is $d_0$-representable; that is, there are convex sets $C_x\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ for $x\in X$ such that, for every $I\subseteq X$, $\bigcap_{x\in I}C_x\neq\varnothing$ if and only if $I$ is contained in some $F\in\mathcal F$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Exists dimension d0 independent of the finite projective plane, with the nerve exactly equal to the subsets of lines.
technical_assessment: Leray/topological lower bounds could obstruct bounded representability, but ordinary homological dimension is only two here and does not give an unbounded lower bound by itself.

statement_utf8: Conjecture 5.9 in [5] asserts that a suitable derivative of every stable rational A-hypergeometric function is a constant multiple of an explicit toric residue. The report states that this conjecture is proved for all codimension-two configurations A.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every stable rational A-hypergeometric function admits a suitable derivative equal to a toric residue; stability, derivative and explicit residue depend on reference 5.
technical_assessment: The literal already reports codimension-two proof; that subcase is not a new outcome. Arbitrary codimension requires the exact residue/classification machinery.

statement_utf8: Let $G=\pi_1^{\mathrm{orb}}(X_0)$, where $X_0=(B^{13}\setminus H)/\Gamma$, $H$ is the union of the mirrors of the triflections, and $\Delta=H/\Gamma$. The quotient obtained from $G$ by requiring a loop around $\Delta$ to have order $2$ is conjectured to be the bimonster $(M\times M):2$, where $M$ is the monster simple group.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: A quotient of a specified orbifold fundamental group should be the bimonster, but Gamma and the mirror arrangement are not defined.
technical_assessment: An arbitrary ball quotient cannot be substituted for Allcock's arrangement; relation computations require the actual lattice and triflections.

statement_utf8:
For every prime $p>2$,
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\frac{\left(\tfrac12\right)_n^3}{n!^3}(4n+1)(-1)^n\equiv \left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)p\pmod{p^3},
\]
where $(a)_n$ is the Pochhammer symbol and $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denotes the Legendre symbol.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every odd prime p; the specified rational sum has the Legendre-symbol value modulo p^3, with denominators prime to p.
technical_assessment: Small exact checks are feasible but cannot prove every prime. This is a classical supercongruence and selected primary-body inspection is required to avoid recounting a known proof.

primary_passage.note: Equation (0.2) is the exact sum and the report explicitly says Mortenson proved it; cited independent proof body not read.

statement_utf8: For every polynomial $f$, every bounded Fatou component of $f$ is a Jordan domain.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every polynomial and every bounded Fatou component; degree restrictions and treatment of rotation domains are not stated.
technical_assessment: Jordan-boundary assertions are sensitive to Siegel and infinitely renormalizable dynamics. A generic local-connectivity heuristic is not a proof for every polynomial.

statement_utf8:
For $d\ge 3$, there exists $C=C(d)\in\mathbb{R}$ such that, for every polynomial $f$ of degree $d$ with an indifferent fixed point at the origin,
\[
\log \operatorname{rad}(f)\le -\frac{1}{d-1}B(\theta)+\log\min_i|c_i|+C,
\]
where the $c_i$ are the critical points of $f$ and $\theta$ is the rotation number at the origin.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each d>=3 exists C(d), every indifferent polynomial at 0; rad(f), B(theta) and the zero-radius convention are not defined.
technical_assessment: Critical-distance normalization and Brjuno small divisors are coupled; quadratic estimates do not give the degree-dependent coefficient in the claim.

statement_utf8: For every transcendental entire function $f$, can every escaping point $z\in I(f)$, where $I(f)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: f^n(z)\to\infty\text{ as }n\to\infty\}$, be connected to $\infty$ by a curve consisting entirely of escaping points?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every transcendental entire f and every escaping z; existence of an escaping curve from z to infinity.
technical_assessment: Dynamic-ray existence for finite-order or bounded-type functions cannot cover all entire functions. Known-counterexample suspicion remains unverified here; no novelty or resolution assertion.

statement_utf8: Any flow $x$ satisfying demands $d$ can be written as a convex combination of unsplittable flows $y^{\ell}$, $\ell\in L$, each satisfying demands $d$ and such that $y^{\ell}_e\le x_e+d_{\max}$ for every $e\in E$, where $d_{\max}=\max_i d_i$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every feasible flow and demand vector, exists convex decomposition with edge excess <=largest demand; topology, source/sink pattern and directedness are missing.
technical_assessment: Single-source path rounding may fail for multicommodity flows. Must restore network hypotheses before proposing a rounding certificate.

statement_utf8: For all $i<j<k$, the constraint $x_{ik}-y_{ijik}-y_{ikjk}+y_{ijjk}=0$ induces a face of the polytope $P_n$. In particular, $QLO(n)$ is a face of $P_n$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every i<j<k; asserted face relation and inclusion of QLO(n), but P_n and its coordinate model are absent.
technical_assessment: Cannot validate a supporting hyperplane without a vertex or inequality definition of P_n. Algebraic cancellation alone is insufficient.

statement_utf8:
For the generalized pinning model with 
\(\alpha=1/2\), equivalently \(K(n)\mathop{\sim}_{n\to\infty} Cn^{-3/2}\) for some \(C>0\), disorder is relevant at marginality: \(h_c(\beta)-h_c^a(\beta)>0\) for every \(\beta>0\). Moreover, there exists \(c>0\) such that
\[
h_c(\beta)-h_c^a(\beta)\ge \exp(-c/\beta^4),\qquad \beta\le 1.
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every beta>0 in a marginal renewal pinning model with K(n)~Cn^-3/2; lower bound for beta<=1, but disorder law and critical points are not defined.
technical_assessment: A beta^-4 rare-stretch argument depends on disorder tails and normalization. Deterministic disorder would alter relevance, so missing model assumptions matter.

statement_utf8: For all convex and twice continuously differentiable potentials \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\), the following assertions hold: (1) each front in the chain corresponds to a conservative shock in the \(p\)-system; (2) for each supersonic conservative shock in the \(p\)-system, there exists a corresponding monotone front in the chain.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every convex C2 potential, all fronts and every supersonic conservative shock; chain, p-system and monotone-front conventions external.
technical_assessment: Conservation identities may prove one implication, but existence in the converse is an infinite-dimensional variational problem. No full two-clause route.

statement_utf8:
For the toy problem (1)–(2) described on the source pages, with spatial variable in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), if \(d\ge 5\), then there exists \(\alpha _0>0\) such that, for every \(\alpha\in(0,\alpha _0)\), the flow has a two-dimensional invariant torus
\[
M=\{(r,U)=(r,U)(\phi):\phi\in\mathbb{T}^2\}
\]
of size \(O(\sqrt{\alpha})\).
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each d>=5 exists alpha0, all small positive alpha; a small invariant two-torus for missing equations (1)-(2).
technical_assessment: Cannot assess resonances, flow or parameters without the toy system. A generic Hopf/torus theorem is not a substitute for checking its hypotheses.

statement_utf8: Does there exist an unbounded number of neighborly triangulations of the 3-torus with vertex-transitive \(\mathbb Z_n\)-symmetry, for \(n\ge 15\), where “neighborly” means that any two vertices are joined by an edge?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Unboundedly many neighborly vertex-transitive cyclic triangulations of T^3 with n>=15 vertices.
technical_assessment: An orbit-of-tetrahedra construction would need links to be spheres and global T^3 identification for unbounded n. A few finite examples give no family mechanism.

statement_utf8: For the Robin boundary-control problem (1)–(3) described in the report, with $T=1.58$, $\b1=1$, and $y_d(x)=\frac{1}{2}(1-x^2)$, the report proves that the optimal control is bang-bang with exactly one switching point $\bar{\tau}\in(1.329,1.3294)$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: One Robin control problem at fixed parameters with a unique switch in the displayed interval, but equations (1)-(3) and a parameter symbol are missing.
technical_assessment: Already described as proved in the report; neither a new theorem nor a self-contained numerical certificate can be recovered without the PDE and cost.

statement_utf8: Let $K$ be an arbitrary field and let $F/K$ be a finitely generated transcendental extension. Then $F$ is fully Hilbertian.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every field K and every finitely generated transcendental F/K; fully Hilbertian is an external strengthened Hilbert property.
technical_assessment: The title itself says Theorem 2; selected primary passage checked. Ordinary Hilbert irreducibility is weaker than the independent-specialization condition and cannot alone bridge it.

primary_passage.note: Definition of fully Hilbertian and Theorem 2 explicitly give this function-field result; no full proof audited.

statement_utf8:
For every integer $n\ge 2$, if $V\subseteq \mathbb A^n$ is a hypersurface defined over $\mathbb Q$ such that $V(\mathbb Q)$ is Zariski dense, then
\[
V(\mathbb Q)\cap\bigl((\mathbb Q\setminus\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb Q^{n-1}\bigr)
\]
is Zariski dense.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every n>=2 and Q-hypersurface with dense rational points; asks density after requiring first coordinate nonintegral.
technical_assessment: Literal x1=0 gives a trivial failure, but this is a missing dominant-coordinate hypothesis or wording correction. Primary question inspected before any proposal; no discovery credit.

primary_passage.note: Conjecture 1 and claimed n=2 consequence read; extracted product/difference notation is defective and does not safely settle the intended coordinate scope.

statement_utf8: For a field $F$, does there exist an integer $n$ depending only on $F$ such that, for every central simple algebra $A$ over $F$, $\operatorname{ind}(A)\mid \operatorname{per}(A)^n$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every field F asks existence of one exponent n(F) working for every central simple F-algebra.
technical_assessment: Allowing arbitrary fields admits unbounded Brauer-dimension constructions; these are classical structural objections, not a small new certificate. Source scope must be checked before any promotion.

statement_utf8: For every number field $K$, does there exist an elliptic curve $E/K$ such that $\operatorname{rank}(E(K))=0$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every number field K, exists elliptic curve E/K with Mordell-Weil rank exactly zero.
technical_assessment: A rational rank-zero curve need not remain rank zero over K. Proving one for each field requires arithmetic rank control beyond a finite search.

statement_utf8:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a domain of finite measure, and let $\lambda_{n}^{\Omega}$ be the $n$-th Dirichlet-Laplacian eigenvalue on $\Omega$, counted with multiplicity. Is it true, without assuming that $\Omega$ is tiling, that
\[
\lambda_{n}^{\Omega}\geq \frac{4\pi}{|\Omega|}\,n
\quad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N}?
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every finite-area planar domain and every positive eigenvalue index n; lower bound 4pi*n/area without a tiling hypothesis.
technical_assessment: Berezin/Li-Yau averaged bounds lose the sharp pointwise constant. Tiling examples or n=1 checks cannot settle arbitrary domains and all indices.

statement_utf8:
Let $d\ge 2$ and let $\gamma>0$ be given. Is there a positive constant $C$ such that
\[
|\lambda|^\gamma\le C\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|V(x)|^{d/2+\gamma}\,dx,
\]
for every complex-valued potential $V\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and every eigenvalue $\lambda\notin\mathbb{R}_+=[0,\infty)$ of the operator $-\Delta+V$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each d>=2,gamma>0 exists C(d,gamma) uniform over compactly supported smooth complex potentials and every nonpositive-axis-excluded eigenvalue.
technical_assessment: Scaling gives the displayed exponent but no uniform resolvent bound near the continuous spectrum. Large-gamma counterexample literature would need exact smooth compact-support scope clearance.

statement_utf8:
For an arbitrary bounded domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), prove that, for all \(m\),
\[
\frac{\lambda_{2m}}{\lambda_m}(\Omega)\leq \frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}(\text{ball in }\mathbb{R}^n).
\]
Here \(\lambda_j\) denotes the \(j\)-th Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplacian on \(\Omega\).
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every dimension n, bounded domain and positive m; doubled-index ratio bounded by the same-dimensional ball first-gap ratio.
technical_assessment: The m=1 PPW theorem does not compare lambda_(2m) and lambda_m. Disconnected unions only reproduce special cases, and no valid all-index interpolation is established.

statement_utf8:
For irrotational travelling water waves 
\((\gamma\equiv 0)\), the profile of any extreme wave has corners with included angle \(120^\circ\) at stagnation points.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All irrotational extreme travelling waves and stagnation points; periodicity, gravity/capillarity and wave regularity class are unstated.
technical_assessment: Classical Stokes-corner theorem is a serious prior objection in standard gravity-wave scope; extending to every interpretation of extreme wave is not justified by the literal.

statement_utf8: Choose the expansion point in rational Krylov-subspace model reduction so as to obtain a good approximation of the system’s response to arbitrary input signals. The report reformulates this as choosing the free Laguerre parameter $\alpha$ in the time-domain reduction method.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Arbitrary input signals but no system class, error norm, tolerance or objective for good approximation.
technical_assessment: No mathematically falsifiable full-scope optimization target; retain without replacement rather than inventing a norm and choosing a numerical parameter.

statement_utf8: **Pisot Substitution Conjecture I.** \(\Lambda\) is a regular model set with windows \(W\) (up to boundary points of the sets \(W_i\)), meaning that \(\Lambda_i=\Lambda_G(W_i)\) for all \(i\), up to points arising from the boundary of \(W_i\).
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every color index i in unspecified Lambda,windows and cut-and-project scheme; substitution and its hypotheses absent.
technical_assessment: Pisot terminology in the title cannot supply irreducibility, unimodularity or the actual internal group. Boundary exceptions also require precise definitions.

statement_utf8:
Let $J=[0,1)=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, let $T:J\to J$ be an interval exchange transformation, and define
$$
\phi_1(x,y)=\liminf_{n\to\infty} n\,\langle T^n(x)-y\rangle,
$$
where $\langle a\rangle=\min_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}|a-k|$. If $T$ is uniquely ergodic, must $\phi_1(x,y)<\infty$ hold for every $x,y\in J$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every uniquely ergodic IET and every ordered x,y in the circle; liminf n*distance finite.
technical_assessment: Almost-everywhere shrinking-target theorems do not yield every pair. A slow-approach counterexample would need exact uniquely ergodic interval-exchange data, not finite orbit sampling.

statement_utf8:
Assume that $n>2$ and that $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{Q}_{<0}$. Then, for every finitely generated $U_c$-module $M$, one has an equality of algebraic cycles
\[
\operatorname{ch}_{GS}(M)=\operatorname{ch}_{GG}(M).
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For all n>2,c outside negative rationals and finitely generated U_c-modules; U_c and both characteristic-cycle constructions are undefined.
technical_assessment: Equality requires comparison of filtrations/localization constructions, not merely agreement on simple examples. No local certificate without the actual algebra and functors.

statement_utf8: For arbitrary \(\mathfrak g\) and \(\ell\), every cluster monomial of \(R_\ell\) is the class of a simple object.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Arbitrary Lie algebra g and ell, every cluster monomial in R_ell; the category, admissible g,ell and cluster seed absent.
technical_assessment: Monoidal categorification can prove such statements only after the intended quantum-affine category and parameter range are fixed. Method similarity is not a subsumption bridge.
